stem:
Tejas colours a $6$-by-$6$ grid in checkerboard black and white, then removes two opposite corner squares that are the same colour. He wants to cover the remaining region with $2 \times 1$ tiles that do not overlap and leave no gaps.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The answer is the word checkerboard, because that colouring word is printed with the grid.
Yes: the remaining region has $34$ squares, an even count, so $2 \times 1$ tiles can cover it.
No: each $2 \times 1$ tile covers one black and one white square, but the remaining region has unequal black and white counts.
The same colouring argument also settles tiling of every even-area shape, including shapes with no grid colouring.

teacher.key_rationale: Removing two same-colour corners leaves unequal black and white counts, so 2×1 tiles cannot cover even though 34 is even. Naming the colouring word swaps the decision for a label. Using even area alone omits the colour balance. Extending the argument to uncoloured shapes over-extends the invariant.
